subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of the following is a leading cause of deforestation in the Amazon rainforest?
questions.explain: Cattle ranching, along with logging, mining and farming, is a major direct cause of Amazon deforestation.

questions.q: Which adaptation helps a cactus survive in a hot desert?
options: Broad, flat leaves to catch rain
A thick, waxy stem to store water
questions.explain: A cactus stores water in its thick, waxy stem and has spines instead of leaves to reduce water loss.

questions.q: In which atmospheric cell does cold air sink at the poles, creating high pressure?
questions.explain: In the Polar cell, very cold dense air sinks at the poles forming high pressure.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the climate of a tropical rainforest?
options: Cold and dry all year round
Hot in summer and cold in winter
Hot and dry all year round
Hot and wet all year round
questions.explain: Tropical rainforests near the Equator are hot and wet throughout the year, with no distinct dry season.

questions.q: Hot deserts are best described as having:
options: Constant cloud cover and high humidity
Low rainfall and large daily temperature ranges
questions.explain: Hot deserts receive very little rain (under 250mm a year) and have hot days but cold nights, giving a large daily temperature range.

questions.q: Tropical storms generally do NOT form right at the equator because:
options: There is too little Coriolis effect to make them spin
The sea is too warm there
questions.explain: The Coriolis effect is near zero at the equator, so storms cannot start spinning.

questions.q: Which is an example of MITIGATION of climate change rather than adaptation?
options: Switching to renewable energy to cut emissions
questions.explain: Mitigation reduces the causes (emissions); adaptation copes with the effects.

questions.q: Which is the strongest piece of EVIDENCE for recent climate change?
options: Rising global average temperatures and shrinking ice sheets
questions.explain: Records of rising temperatures, melting ice and sea-level rise evidence climate change.

questions.q: The most intense winds and heaviest rain in a tropical storm occur in the:
questions.explain: The eyewall, the ring of towering clouds around the eye, has the strongest winds and rain.

questions.q: In a tropical rainforest, the dense, continuous layer of treetops that blocks most light from reaching the ground is called the:
questions.explain: The canopy is a thick layer of treetops about 30–45m up that absorbs most of the sunlight and rainfall.

questions.q: In the Hadley cell, air at the equator rises because it is:
options: Warm and rising, creating low pressure
questions.explain: Intense equatorial heating makes air rise, forming a low-pressure belt with heavy rain.

questions.q: What is the role of producers in a food chain?
options: They convert sunlight into energy by photosynthesis
They recycle nutrients into the soil
questions.explain: Producers such as green plants make their own food from sunlight through photosynthesis, forming the base of the food chain.
